newsitem.title: USA: Four added to jury pool in secondhand smoke trial.
newsitem.headline: Four added to jury pool in secondhand smoke trial.

text.p: A postal worker and a power-utility employee were among four people added on Thursday to a pool of prospective jurors for a landmark trial focusing on the effects of breathing secondhand cigarette smoke.

A total of 104 people have passed initial screening by lawyers searching for six jurors and 10 alternates to hear testimony in the $5 billion class-action lawsuit. The case was brought on behalf of thousands of non-smoking flight attendants, whose tobacco-related ailments were allegedly caused by passengers smoking aboard U.S. airlines.
About 125 people are being sought for the standby pool. A court official said testimony in the trial is unlikely to begin before July 14. Testimony is expected to continue for eight weeks or longer.
